analyst_view.overall: A relegation-zone game: Telstar (16th, 10 pts) host PEC Zwolle (13th, 12 pts), both within a few points of the drop. Telstar ended a ten-game winless run with a 4-2 win over Utrecht and drew 2-2 at Fortuna; coach Henk Brugge, who spent twelve years at PEC, has bought time, and NH Nieuws (19 Nov) reports Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes fit again, while Jelani Seedorf is doubtful after an injury in a friendly. PEC are unbeaten in four and this is Alex Pastoor's first league game since he took over on 9 November; they miss Krastev, Rahajaan and now midfielder Gilles van der Wal, with full-back Floranus 50/50. The numbers still count Alders and Mendes as out; referee Joey Kooij's 3.4 cards a game is already in.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, counting Mendes out for Telstar (-3.5%) and defender Alders out (+6% for PEC). NH Nieuws says both are fit, which would add a little to Telstar's attack and take a little off PEC's, about -1% net, while PEC lose Van der Wal and Telstar may miss Seedorf; these small changes cancel, and both sides concede plenty (counted), so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Telstar's recent drop (25 in six) already counted. Pastoor has said the squad needs little changing, and Telstar's wing play through Martha and Brouwer is what they have shown all season, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already including Joey Kooij's above-average record (+11%) and PEC's slightly busier recent card count. It is a tense six-pointer near the bottom, but that is normal at this end of the table and no bans or flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already lifted for Telstar's busy recent shooting (+11%), led by Tyrone Owusu's four goals in six. Mendes returning adds an option but not a big change in volume, so I stay at 30.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, with both sides' recent accuracy close to normal. A new coach's first league game can be cautious, but Pastoor is keeping the side that went four unbeaten, so I see no reason to move and stay at 10.6.
